items.title: John Batiste "Bat" Stecklet Interview, 1959-06-15
items.q: Well, what did the men, who were the men in that beside you, Mr. Stackler? Who played in that beside you? ... With Johnny Schenk. ... And then I'd play corners with him

ctx.x: lot younger man than I was. I couldn't tell you his age, but I do know that he was a much younger man than I was. Did he come from about the same part of town, downtown here? Yes. Well, I know somewhere between the Leeson Field and, say, El Manasio over here. Well, what they call it now, they changed the name to Franklin Avenue. Franklin Avenue. Franklin Avenue. And then it runs back from the, way up from the beginning near the river to back here where the, where Franklin Avenue turns off this way. Yeah. And the…
Uh, you played, you played with Johnny Schenk. Yeah. Is that right? Yeah. Well, what did the men, who were the men in that beside you, Mr. Stackler? Who played in that beside you?

With Johnny Schenk. Well, Johnny Schenk. Well, nine times out of ten, the fellow John Deveread, uh, John Deveread, he used to play bass with him. And Johnny Williamson, he used to play guitar with him. Uh-huh. And he used to play violin. And then I'd play corners with him, you see? Uh-huh. But, uh, to tell you the truth, now, for a fellow keeping time with a bass fiddle, you understand? Playing dance music, or two-fourth time, or three-fourth time, any time, or six-eighth time, he was the best man that I ever…
